prompt.en: Which word means more than one?

stages.choice_rule: Four lowercase words. Exactly one correct irregular plural of the noun named in the stem. Always include that singular and a regular -s or -es trap. The fourth choice is a close misspelling or a wrong form from this skill. Shuffle answer_index across the pool. Never use another valid plural of the same noun. Never use fishes when the target is fish.

gold_items.stem: What is more than one child?
What is more than one foot?
What is more than one tooth?
Pick the word for many little mouse.
Pick the word for many brown goose.
What is more than one sheep?

roots: Four whole-word choices. One correct irregular plural. Never two valid answers.
Always include the singular and the regular -s or -es form as traps.
The fourth choice is a close misspelling or a wrong irregular from this skill, not a random noun.
Never put the correct plural in the stem except same-form nouns such as sheep or fish.
Do not use kids, people, or friends as a distractor next to children.
Do not use fishes when the target is fish. Use fishs or fishe-like misses instead.
Tier 1: name the singular in a short what-is-more-than-one stem and attach that noun lemma.
Tier 2: use pick-the-word or a NAME saw stem. The main trap is the regular -s form.
Tier 3: same-form plurals or two-syllable vowel changes such as woman to women and leaf to leaves.
Cover child, foot, tooth, mouse, goose, man, woman, leaf, sheep, fish, person, and wolf across the pool.
Stems use only the roots word list, allowed_extra_words, and <NAME>. No real names.
Never describe a picture in the stem. Pictures are lemma notes only. No audio files.

tier_rules.1: Short six-word stems that name one kid-world noun. Picture lemma of that noun. Distractors are the singular and a clear fake -s form.
tier_rules.2: Grade-level stems of six to eight words. Main trap is the regular -s or -es form. Mix animals, body words, and people words.
tier_rules.3: Near-miss items: sheep and fish stay the same, or woman to women and leaf to leaves. Close misspellings sit next to the regular trap.

children.ko: 하나는 child입니다. 둘 이상은 childs가 아니라 children입니다.
